title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། འེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 192)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio of a pramāṇa commentary on omniscience (staff/staff-bearer argument, non-perception of the pervader), consistent with the Tshad ma section of the Tengyur.

ocr_errors.image: ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པའི་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་བྱ་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་ (as far as I can read it)
ocr_errors.problem: ཤེས་བྱ 'knowable' apparently written as homophone ཞེས་བྱ 'called'; both translations follow the OCR ('called the cognition' / garbled phrase)

ocr_errors.image: particles in this gloss are hard to read; ordering of སྟེ/ནི may differ
ocr_errors.problem: possible particle slip; does not change meaning

tr_errors_A.english: <meta>continues from previous page: since birth is impossible, it would absurdly follow that one must investigate them as omniscient.</meta>
tr_errors_A.problem: the page's first sentence is translated only inside the <meta> wrapper, so a reader who does not see meta loses it

tr_errors_A.english: it is said: "Because this is omniscient," and so forth
tr_errors_A.problem: the quoted root lemma is 'This one is omniscient'; 'Because' is added and misframes the lemma

tr_errors_A.english: an observer who has all phenomena as their object cannot ascertain it
tr_errors_A.problem: the subject is the cognition that has all things as object (which cannot be ascertained), not an 'observer'

tr_errors_A.english: that qualifier is also absent in this case
tr_errors_A.problem: what is absent is the apprehension of the qualifier (the pervader), not the qualifier itself

tr_errors_B.english: it would follow that everything must be examined as being omniscience itself
tr_errors_B.problem: ཐམས་ཅད་ is part of the compound ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ 'omniscient' and is also rendered separately as 'everything'

tr_errors_B.english: being empty of that means being an omniscient being
tr_errors_B.problem: literal rendering of an elliptical gloss reads as a self-contradiction (one empty of the omniscient's knowledge is 'an omniscient being'); the sense is that the knowledge one is empty of is that of the omniscient

tr_errors_B.english: for anyone who does not determine the omniscient one because they do not presently perceive everything
tr_errors_B.problem: drops ཉེ་བ 'near/present' (the person in the omniscient's presence) and recasts the clause as a causal one

tr_errors_B.english: Since that individual is both that very person and that very knowledge
tr_errors_B.problem: awkward misparse of the karmadhāraya gloss; still recoverable

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error; A hides the first sentence in <meta> and misframes the root lemma, while B garbles the 'empty of that' gloss and drops 'near' in the last clause, so they come out roughly even.

book_verdict: A correct Derge Tengyur pramāṇa folio. The OCR is close to the print. Both English versions follow the argument faithfully, with only moderate and minor slips; no on-sight defect.
